It’s been a rough year, doc. I’ve just felt… heavy. There are days I just can’t bring myself to start anything, even at work. My mind feels like sludge, and focusing on schematics or designs is nearly impossible. I end up just staring at my screen, feeling drained after just a few minutes of trying to concentrate. I’ve been crying a lot, too, often for no real reason, just sudden bursts of tears I can’t hold back. And honestly, sometimes I just think, "I wish I wasn't here," or "I just want it to end." I don't have a plan, but the thoughts are there.

Then, about a month ago, things shifted. I suddenly had this surge of energy. I was working on four different projects at once, pulling all-nighters and feeling completely fine, like sleep wasn't even necessary. My thoughts were racing, and I couldn't stop talking – just felt this need to fill every silence. There were times I’d be pacing my apartment, wringing my hands, just this restless energy I couldn’t burn off. My mood was all over the place too; one minute I’d feel on top of the world, and the next I’d snap at someone for the smallest thing. It was intense, and honestly, a bit jarring, especially after feeling so low for so long. It was after... that incident years ago, things never quite went back to normal, but these ups and downs feel different.
D009-D018_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

My ex-husband used to say I was "on a mission." My fuse is so short during these times; even the smallest thing, a wrong word from a client, would set me off. And I barely sleep. A couple of hours feels like plenty, and I'm up and at it. It doesn’t really mess up my work, though; if anything, I'm more productive, just… intense. I once had a bad car accident a few years back, and sometimes I wonder if that’s got something to do with all this, but it’s hard to say.

D009-D018_h023.question:
Alright doc, thanks for seeing me. It’s been… a year and some change since I really felt like myself. Before that, for about three months, I was on fire. I was cracking cases left and right, barely sleeping – maybe three, four hours tops – but I woke up feeling great, ready to go. My ex-wife even said I was like a different person, full of ideas, though I guess I snapped at her a lot in those days.

But then that pretty much just… stopped. Now, it's like everything's in slow motion. I used to love the thrill of a tough case, but now it's all just… flat. No excitement, no satisfaction, even when I close one. Getting out of bed feels like I'm moving through molasses, and sometimes I just stare at the wall for what feels like hours. My movements feel heavy, like my limbs are weighted down. It’s hard to focus, and I just feel… numb, you know? Like all my emotions are turned down to a whisper. It definitely makes doing my job a hell of a lot harder. I think a lot about that shooting a couple of years back, the one where I almost didn't make it out. It comes back to me, especially when I'm trying to sleep now.

D009-D018_h024.question:
"I just feel... strange. For the past three months, I’ve had this incredible buzz, you know? Like, I could conquer the world. I don't need much sleep at all – I’ll be up for days working on projects or just decluttering my apartment at 3 AM. It doesn't bother me; I feel fantastic, full of life, even though I'm still single and my job as a content moderator is pretty intense, seeing all that violence. But it's not actually affecting my work, I just feel... good.

Then there are these other times. For over a year now, sometimes, it’s like a switch flips. It’s hard to describe, but it feels like there’s nothing inside. I’ll just sit there, sometimes for a long time, watching the screen, and even really positive feedback at work means nothing to me. When someone asks me a question, it’s like my brain just… slows down. The words are there, but getting them out feels like moving through thick mud. Thinking, focusing, it just drains me instantly. It’s exhausting, and it makes everything so much harder."

D009-D018_h025.question:
I'm not sure where to start, doc. It’s been… a long haul. Over a year now, I guess. Most days, I just feel… nothing. Like an empty room inside me. I don’t care about the shop anymore, even though I built it up myself, brick by brick after Ellen passed. It used to be my pride and joy, but now when customers praise my cuts or the quality of the meat, it just goes right through me. Doesn’t matter. I’m tired all the time, a real bone-deep exhaustion, even lifting a side of beef feels like a mountain. I find myself pacing, picking at my cuticles until they bleed, just can’t sit still even though I’m so worn out.

Then, about three months ago, things shifted. I started getting this irritation, like a raw nerve. Someone asks me a simple question, and I snap. My lads at the shop, they look at me like I’ve grown a second head. I’ve been working non-stop, really. Staying up for days, prepping orders, drawing up new specials at 3 AM. I don’t feel tired at all, just buzz with energy. I’ve probably gotten more done in the last few weeks than in the last year, but it's not normal for me. It’s not causing me issues at work, but it’s definitely not me. I just… I don’t know what’s happening to me. It all started some time after Ellen… after she passed. That was a rough time.
D009-D018_h025.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D009-D018_h025.answer: B & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
